title: GreenCheck: automated VPC API & model smoke harness for post-deploy validation
creator: Aisha Mohan
description:
Summary: GreenCheck is an automated post-deploy validation harness for Private (VPC) deployments. It validates API readiness, model artifact availability, minimal model load behavior, and a short smoke test end-to-end scenario. The harness is intended to run automatically as a final stage of our Terraform apply pipeline and as a periodic health-monitoring job in the customer's control plane.

Scope:
- Validate control plane and data plane endpoints created by Terraform (API gateway, health endpoints, auth)
- Confirm model artifacts download/unpack and minimal inference loop (cold start + small inference)
- Perform a lightweight load exercise to verify batching and KV cache priming for typical short sequences (<=128 tokens)
- Execute a canonical smoke scenario exercising streaming and function/tool-calling surface to detect integration regressions

Inputs from IaC:
- Terraform outputs consumed by the harness: public_api_url, internal_api_url, admin_token_secret_arn, model_bucket_path, instance_group_ids
- The harness reads the deployment manifest to select one stable model variant and one fallback variant for the smoke path

Health checks performed:
1) API readiness: curl ${public_api_url}/v1/health -> expect 200 and JSON {"status":"ready"} within 5s. Retries: 3 with exponential backoff.
2) Auth sanity: request a short token using admin_token and call /v1/whoami to ensure RBAC and SSO mapping succeed.
3) Model pull & local load: trigger model fetch via control-plane endpoint (/admin/load-model?path=...) and poll model-status until STATE==READY or timeout 180s. Capture logs and stack traces on failure.
4) Minimal inference (cold): POST /v1/generate small prompt ("Hello"), ensure HTTP 200, token stream begins within 500ms of first chunk, and final tokens length > 1.
5) KV/cache priming check: run 10 sequential short requests with shared session id and assert tail latency decreases or stays stable (no >2x variance) after 3rd request.
6) Smoke scenario: simulated user conversation with tool call (function call) to validate structured output routing and function invocation path.
7) Lightweight load exercise: 30 parallel single-token generation requests spread across instance group; verify no instance reports >90% GPU memory during test and p95 latency under 1s for single-token responses.

Acceptance criteria:
- All checks pass in <6 minutes in a normal healthy environment.
- If model fails to reach READY, mark deployment as FAILED and run a diagnostic bundle (logs, kernel selection profile, recent OOM traces) uploaded to S3 for on-call inspection.
- Harness should emit structured events to the console dashboard: greencheck.succeeded|failed with failure_reason tag and relevant metrics.

Rollback & mitigation policy:
- If API readiness fails: abort rollout and mark PR/Terraform run as FAILED. Notify on-call via Slack channel #infra-deploys.
- If model load fails but API is ready: attempt a single automated retry with a different variant (fallback) then fail if still unsuccessful.

Implementation notes:
- The harness is implemented as a small Go binary run as part of the Terraform pipeline (step: post-apply-validate) and as a Lambda (or k8s job) for periodic runs.
- Uses Terraform remote state to resolve outputs; config is parameterized so customers can opt-out of automated model pulls in air-gapped installs.
- Metrics emitted via Prometheus pushgateway and events to the console event bus for visibility in rollout dashboards.
- Diagnostic bundle format and S3 path follow /redwood-diagnostics/private/{deployment_id}/{timestamp}.tar.gz

Security considerations:
- Admin token used by the harness is rotated per deployment and stored in KMS-backed secret. Requests are made from a temporary ephemeral runner within the VPC.
- When security_review_required is true, the harness will not run automated model-pull unless customer approved opt-in is present in their deployment manifest.

Operational runbook (high level):
- Step 1: Inspect harness logs at the pipeline job and diagnostics S3 bundle.
- Step 2: If model pull failed, check network ACLs, S3 permissions, and instance role IAM policy.
- Step 3: If memory pressure observed, trigger an autoscale to bring up another instance group and re-run the greencheck on demand.
